summary: How Adolf Hitler and the Nazi state ran on drugs: Hitler's quack physician Theodor Morell dosed him with stimulants, opioids and animal hormones from 1936 to 1945, while the Wehrmacht fought its blitzkrieg campaigns on methamphetamine.

evidence.note: segment on Weimar-era drug culture in Berlin and German drug law
extended critique of Ohler's book and its claims about Nazi drug policy
Morell's vitamin injections secretly spiked with stimulants and hormones
1936: Morell treats Hoffmann and is introduced to Hitler, start of main span
Morell revives Czech president Hacha during the 1939 annexation talks
Pervitin's first battlefield use in the 1939 invasion of Poland
tens of millions of meth pills issued for the 1940 invasion of France
meth use and its collapse in effectiveness during the invasion of Russia
Hitler's isolation at the Wolf's Lair in East Prussia, today in Poland
Morell begins Eukodal (oxycodone) injections in July 1943
after the 1944 bomb plot, Giesing gives Hitler repeated cocaine treatments
Morell runs out of drugs, is expelled from the bunker in 1945, dies after the war

notes: Topical deep-dive, not a biography: the story actually covers roughly 1918-1945 (Weimar drug culture to the bunker). covered_span starts at 1889 only because the lifetime rule requires Hitler's birth year. Morell arguably deserves co-primary status given his airtime; kept secondary since the title centres Hitler. Wikidata omitted for Morell (not certain of QID).
